verdict.summary: Anyone can register an OAuth app in minutes and let any user authorize it, with no GitHub review. The friction is organization approval for org data, and Marketplace review only if you want a listing.
verdict.approval_wait: none (Marketplace listing only: about 2-6 weeks, community-reported)

steps.title: Decide: managed auth or your own app
steps.detail: Composio offers managed OAuth for GitHub, so you can start there. Register your own app only if you need your own client ID and secret, branding, or token policy. GitHub also recommends GitHub Apps for new integrations.

steps.title: Get the Composio callback URL
steps.detail: Create a GitHub auth config in Composio and copy the callback URL it shows.
gotchas: The catalog shows a v1 callback path and a probe used v3; use the one Composio displays.

steps.title: Open Developer settings
steps.detail: Go to Developer settings > OAuth Apps and click New OAuth App (Register a new application for a first app).

steps.title: Fill in the registration form
steps.detail: Enter the application name, homepage URL, optional description, and the authorization callback URL. Use only public information in these fields.

values.label: Redirect URI
values.value: Composio callback URL (see the Composio callout on this page)

gotchas: You can add up to 10 callback URLs with Add callback URL.

steps.title: Generate a client secret and add to Composio
steps.detail: Copy the client ID and generate a client secret, then enter both in your Composio auth config.

steps.title: Choose minimal scopes
steps.detail: Pick only the scopes you need. Composio's default set (repo, user, gist, notifications, project, workflow, codespace) is broad. Users see the requested scopes on the authorization form and can edit them later.

steps.title: Decide on token expiry
steps.detail: Expiring tokens (8-hour access token, six-month refresh token) are on by default for new apps. Make sure your integration refreshes tokens.

steps.title: Connect your own account
steps.detail: Run a test authorization through Composio with your own GitHub account.

steps.title: Get organization approval for org data
steps.detail: Users who need org resources request access, and an org owner approves the app under OAuth app access restrictions. Org owners can limit who may request apps.
gotchas: Approval is org-wide, not per repository.

steps.title: Request a rate-limit increase if needed
steps.detail: Watch the 2,000 token-requests-per-hour limit. Rate-limit increases are granted per OAuth app.

steps.title: Optional: Marketplace listing
steps.detail: Only needed for a listing. Prepare contact details, description, pricing plan, privacy policy link, support link, logo and screenshots. Accept the Marketplace Developer Agreement and click Request publish.

steps.title: Optional: Publisher verification
steps.detail: Needed only for paid plans or a Marketplace badge. Apply under Publisher Verification in the org's Developer settings, then wait for GitHub's review.

requirements.item: Application name, homepage URL, callback URL
requirements.detail: Required on the registration form; description is optional.
Required for the app to access private org resources when access restrictions are on.
Public app, privacy policy link, support contact, pricing plan, logo and screenshots.
Org you own, contact details, 2FA, verified domain. Only for paid plans or a badge.

scopes.effect: Full read/write on public and private repos. GitHub docs mark no extra review for it.
Lets the token update GitHub Actions workflow files.
Lets the token create and manage codespaces.
Can be used in testing to request expiring tokens with refresh tokens.

blockers.symptom: App cannot reach private org resources
blockers.cause: OAuth app access restrictions are on and the app is unapproved.
blockers.fix: Ask an org owner to approve the app.

blockers.symptom: Cannot request the app in an org
blockers.cause: The org limits app requests to members only or to no one.
blockers.fix: Ask an org owner to change the setting or approve directly.

blockers.symptom: Users are asked to re-authorize, or token generation is blocked
blockers.cause: Ten sign-ins in an hour, or the 2,000 token requests per hour limit.
blockers.fix: Reuse tokens and avoid repeated sign-ins; request a rate-limit increase.

blockers.symptom: Cannot sign in to a private or internal app
blockers.cause: Only members of the owning org or enterprise can sign in.
blockers.fix: Test with a member account or make the app public.

composio.note: Start on Composio's managed OAuth to skip registration. Register your own app only if you need your own client ID and secret, branding, or token policy. Composio's default scopes are broad, so request fewer in your own app. Confirm the callback path (v1 vs v3) in Composio before registering.

open_questions: No install or user cap for unlisted OAuth apps was found; the only approval gate found is organization approval.
No official OAuth app review process was found; Marketplace timing is community-sourced only.
The scope docs do not mark any scopes as sensitive or restricted requiring extra review.
Composio's default callback differs between the v1 catalog path and the v3 path; confirm in Composio.
Rate limits for non-Enterprise-Cloud app-owned requests beyond 5,000 per hour were not confirmed.
